summary: I forwarded all 17 spec-gap findings verbatim to the Microarch agent in one call. It returned no_patch (exit code 1) with no revised spec and no owner decisions, and gave no reason. I then escalated all 17 to a human. The escalation covers four things: the unexplained no_patch result, the owner decisions the findings need, the spec-revision mismatch between the findings and the current spec, and the unvalidated drop. I used 1 of 3 dispatches and kept 2 in reserve. I made no RTL fixes and no spec revisions.

actions.reason: All 17 spec-gap findings were forwarded verbatim to the Microarch agent in one call. It returned status=no_patch, exit_code=1, revised_spec=null, and no owner_decisions, so no compiler patch was proposed and nothing was recompiled. It gave no reason, so I can't tell whether this was a tool failure or a refusal. Several gaps are owner decisions: unmapped_read_data, unmapped_write_behavior, access_violation_error, read_byte_enable_semantics, status_read_sampling, speculative_activate, and the ref_pending_cnt width versus max_postpone cap. Validation's handoff proposes values for some, but I won't choose them myself. The block_interfaces gap is marked deferred in the handoff. The findings are tagged with spec revision golden_ddr3_1600k_x8_2lane_1rank, but the current spec is compiled_ddr3800_x8_1lane_1rank. Validation also did not run on this drop (validated_this_drop=False), so the findings may be stale. A human should check why the Microarch agent produced no patch, make the owner decisions, and decide whether to re-run validation. I have 2 dispatches left and held them back rather than retry blindly.
